The core insight is that perception is not a passive process but an active construction of sensory data into meaningful visual fields. The optical diagram coalescence primitive formalizes how sensation and object perception merge under normal vision, expressed mathematically as \( \mathcal{P}(\text{visual}) = \mathcal{S}_{\text{assign}} \cap \mathcal{S}_{\text{object}} \). This implies that perception is a set intersection of two sensory streams, which only aligns under ideal conditions. The artist’s attentional focus diverges from the layman’s by dwelling on the signs themselves rather than their implications, captured by \( \mathcal{A}_{\text{artist}} = \int_{\text{signs}} \mathcal{L}(\text{signs}) d\text{space} \). The normal vision situation introduces a transformational framework where perception is normalized through viewing conditions, \( \mathcal{V}_{\text{normal}} = \mathcal{V}_{\text{real}} \circ \mathcal{T}_{\text{view}}^{-1} \). These primitives form a dual structure: one for perceptual alignment and another for attentional modulation, both critical to GSI's Bayesian inference and GSE's situational reasoning.
